title: Rig DAG dashboard: render beads as a git-graph-style pipeline
description: New rig-scoped view rendering the bead dependency graph (parent/child, blocks) as a terminal DAG in the style of 'git log --graph', showing beads flowing toward the refinery/merge stage. Motivated by live-debugging the refinery-not-merging issue: want a visual read on exactly where beads are stuck in the pipeline instead of scanning flat lists.
acceptance_criteria: new subcommand (e.g. 'oil-cop dag <rig>') renders a DAG using dependency data already available from 'bd list' (parent, dependencies[], blocks/parent-child types); the refinery/merge stage is visually distinct so a stuck merge is obvious at a glance; works as a one-shot render and inside 'watch' for live updates; --json emits the graph structure (nodes+edges) for scripting.
close_reason: Done. New 'oil-cop dag <rig>' command (+ folded into 'watch <rig>'): renders beads as a tree/git-graph via parent/child, with 'blocked by' annotations for cross-tree blocks edges. --json emits nodes with parent/blocked_by for scripting. Verified live against luminate (84 nodes, correct tree grouping under epics like luminate-2vr/bgb/wl7/lpm) -- and it immediately surfaced luminate-bjj ('polecats close beads without pushing branches -- completed work strands locally, never reaches master'), which is exactly the refinery-not-merging bug motivating this bead.

title: Animate DAG bead states: red -> yellow (flashing) -> green
description: Bead-lifecycle-specific color state machine for the DAG view (distinct from the existing staleness-based Health palette used in status/queue/agents): open/ready beads render red, in_progress beads render yellow and flash/pulse on each watch tick, and beads that reach closed/merged render green and go static. Gives an at-a-glance read of which beads are actively moving vs stuck vs done.
acceptance_criteria: DAG node color follows red (open/ready/blocked) -> yellow (in_progress) -> green (closed/merged); yellow nodes visibly flash/alternate each watch refresh tick; green nodes are static once merged; works with --no-color/non-tty fallback (e.g. bracketed state label) same as the rest of the tool.
close_reason: Done. BeadStage enum (Pending/Active/Merged) + bead_stage_glyph in render/color.rs: red for pending, yellow flashing (alternates bold/plain each watch tick) for active, green static for merged. Also added a 'landed_unmerged' flag (via GitAdapter) for in_progress beads whose branch already merged into target in git -- the stuck-refinery signal. Verified color codes via pty capture (31m red / 1;33m bold yellow / 32m green) and JSON stage classification against live luminate data.

title: Segment gc/bd/dolt adapters behind a common trait
description: src/sources/gc.rs and bd.rs are ad hoc wrappers called directly from assemble.rs/main.rs. Extract a shared adapter trait/interface (e.g. a RigDataSource-style trait covering: city status, rig list/status, bead list/status) with gc and bd as the first two implementations. Purpose: make room for a dedicated adapter for the gastown pack specifically (or any other pack) without touching render/assemble/model code — mirrors how Gas City itself is pack-extensible.
acceptance_criteria: src/sources/ restructured around a trait implemented per tool (gc, bd); assemble.rs and main.rs call the trait, not concrete gc::/bd:: functions directly; adding a stub third adapter requires no changes outside sources/; existing status/queue/agents/watch commands behave identically after the refactor (verified against the live carbon-city).
close_reason: Done. src/sources/adapters.rs adds GcAdapter/BdAdapter/GitAdapter traits + CliGc/CliBd/LocalGit impls + an Adapters bundle; assemble/render/main now depend only on the traits. Dropped the planned Dolt adapter per oilcop-bb9.4's finding, added a small GitAdapter (merge-ancestry check) instead. Verified: status/queue/agents behave identically against live carbon-city after the refactor; 0 clippy warnings.

comments.author: david awad
comments.text: Per oilcop-bb9.4's finding: dropping a Dolt adapter from scope. Trait implementations will be gc, bd, and a new small git adapter (branch/merge-ancestry checks for the DAG's refinery stage) instead.

title: DAG dashboard + pack-agnostic tool adapters
description: Two related asks: (1) segment oil-cop's gc/bd/dolt integrations behind a common adapter interface, mirroring Gas City's own pack-based extensibility, so a separate gastown-pack-specific adapter (or others) can plug in without touching render/assemble code. (2) a rig-scoped dashboard that renders beads as a live git-graph-style DAG moving through the refinery, with red->yellow(flashing)->green state coloring, motivated by live-debugging the current refinery-not-merging issue.
close_reason: Epic complete: adapters refactored (gc/bd/git traits), dag dashboard shipped, bead-stage color animation shipped. Dolt adapter scoped out and dropped per investigation.

comments.author: david awad
comments.text: All four children done. Bonus: the dag command's first real run against luminate immediately surfaced luminate-bjj, which describes the exact refinery-not-merging symptom -- polecats closing beads without pushing branches. That bead + the new landed_unmerged flag together are a decent starting point for actually debugging it.

title: Investigate whether a direct Dolt adapter is needed for refinery/merge state
description: bd list already returns per-bead metadata (branch, work_dir, gc.work_branch, gc.session_id etc) and gc exposes 'gc dolt health --json'. Before building a real Dolt (SQL) adapter, check whether this existing metadata plus gc's own commands is sufficient to show refinery/merge state in the DAG (bead C depends on knowing this), or whether direct Dolt access (commit graph, merge/PR status) is genuinely required. Write up the finding as a bead comment/decision either way.
acceptance_criteria: clear yes/no decision recorded (as a bead comment or a decision-type note) on whether a raw Dolt adapter is needed; if yes, scope is captured in a follow-up bead; if no, the adapter trait from bead A only needs gc+bd implementations for now.
close_reason: Investigated: no Dolt adapter needed; bd status + metadata already model the pipeline. Replacing planned scope with a small git adapter for branch/merge-ancestry checks instead — folded into bead A.

comments.author: david awad
comments.text:
Finding: no raw Dolt (SQL) adapter needed.

Checked live data against carbon-city/luminate:
- bd's own bead status already models the pipeline: open/blocked -> in_progress -> closed. Closed already means merged for a normal task bead.
- bd has a "merge-request" issue type built in (bd list --type merge-request) for a distinct refinery queue, though luminate has none open right now.
- Every in-progress bead's metadata already carries `branch` (e.g. "polecat/luminate-2vr.2") and `gc.work_branch` (target, e.g. "master") via `bd list`/`bd show` -- no Dolt query required to get this.
- `gc dolt health --json` exists but is coarse (server up/down, commits/open_beads per db) -- not per-bead merge state, not useful for the DAG specifically.
- gc's actual merge primitive is "gc convoy land" (closes a convoy once all children are closed) -- again bead-status-driven, not something needing direct Dolt access.

Decision: skip a Dolt adapter. To diagnose "stuck at refinery" specifically (bead in_progress with a branch that hasn't actually been merged into its work_branch yet), the useful addition is a small local git adapter -- check merge-base/ancestry of metadata.branch against metadata.gc.work_branch in the rig's own working directory. That's a git concern, not a Dolt one. Folding this into bead A's adapter trait as a third adapter (gc, bd, git) instead of a dolt one.
